body:
| | | [](http://links.makingamericathegreatest.com/u/click?_t=79fa4a3daf024a0a886c5b498ff32e32&_m=01208e16dbd1403e8dbedb08129441e7&_e=ciw7abm-rOia2M7TJmU8QUCMCIaNeTdfoJ09H_o3RasJu6S-BVezgRAslPWVhQ5VWtxz0J66uQj8hEhPIaiVCaAMwkxQDpBiP8gAf8zEbvVMbCG_W6usKbmX7nGuJnoKRBOR3BIF_N8aA7N67n2KsnIvgtr6UGsMvczAaYVvLZi9bqWL1GwliiXzWSckJme9OfU2C-LWq-0o0MXl0MvsG7uaR_6hEo7ilnF39kr4wI2Z3RnoeskYNzuTRotyzswzqM_eRuOaluGUnkG5eDtQ9mrX5HLfPt96jwcAn3fJ0yWecgyzCrey-FjIS-pUZ1ewFmwByVThZ7iKs9t8SVW-B5OyUooZSH7zKSfPlYQ0YKlGUIUC8-eSggSz_caOWb4_RMk3EEPTxw9tw4GLQgvpMb92n6OkmxMYxGxBN_yFwln6IH8CVDYryrYEDV49OXeaYJfrTES3Li5hmhEjgETtgJMnUGoRxzw8EYp8H3jrT0jnMyTZgr--RNMGGtkKz-Mv71KaqUgT3jTR4QtcKudnR6tZcfj4CR2NfUyZg_eLE0xVr--ukZq-rN5g8__Y3v_eqTyGruz6KgjJZrlS0VwXCS5CVil62m7UQevd4e_5FngdbIXjDxIdazQ1oBwqqnisOkaQ-gpprtZS-6LGzp_Alw1PHFA6CAd7-2ZkySj7xnUC1rfrbgLVMbfd02xbTRwas9Qj2-2czOsJzDmcE8zsdUlCyHsIgk1aNYTDDmYNdDY%3D)
---
| | Friend,
---
If you ever doubted we could win America's youth back from the Left...

If you ever wondered whether we'd lost the next generation for good...

If you ever sat up at night -- watching the news, seeing what's happening in our schools, our culture, our country -- and thought, _" Is it already too late?" _

You're not alone.

A lot of good people have been asking the same question.

**But I want to tell you something that might just change how you feel about the future of this country... **

Just one year ago, Turning Point USA's high school program -- which is now called "Club America" -- was in about 1,200 schools.

That was no small feat.

Starting a single chapter today takes serious courage. Students get mocked. Threatened. Investigated. Sometimes even physically attacked.

So reaching 1,200 chapters already felt like a miracle.

_Then Charlie called me... _

He said: "Andrew, I love what we're doing with our high school program -- but we've got to move faster."

I told him, "We are."

Charlie replied, "No you're not thinking what I'm thinking... I want to be in 35,000 high schools."

I laughed. I told him, "Charlie, there aren't even 35,000 high schools in America."

"Okay," he said, "How many are there?"

"About 27,000."

Without skipping a beat, Charlie said, "Okay, great. Let's do 27,000!"
I'll be honest -- I froze.

We didn't have the numbers. We didn't have the staff. We didn't have the roadmap yet.

But he wasn't fazed.

He said, "Don't worry. We'll figure it out. We'll do it together."

That was Charlie.

He didn't think small. He didn't move slow. He didn't settle for "maybe someday."

He believed in going now.

And he believed that if the mission was right, the path would reveal itself.

He chased what others only dreamed about... and turned what others thought impossible into reality.

That's why he built Turning Point USA in the first place.

That's why tens of thousands of students were inspired by Charlie to start chapters of their own -- _many in schools where they were explicitly told not to. _

**And that 's why today -- less than a year later -- we're not in 1,200 schools anymore: **
---
[](http://links.makingamericathegreatest.com/u/click?_t=79fa4a3daf024a0a886c5b498ff32e32&_m=01208e16dbd1403e8dbedb08129441e7&_e=ciw7abm-rOia2M7TJmU8QUCMCIaNeTdfoJ09H_o3RasJu6S-BVezgRAslPWVhQ5VWtxz0J66uQj8hEhPIaiVCaAMwkxQDpBiP8gAf8zEbvVMbCG_W6usKbmX7nGuJnoKRBOR3BIF_N8aA7N67n2KsnIvgtr6UGsMvczAaYVvLZi9bqWL1GwliiXzWSckJme9OfU2C-LWq-0o0MXl0MvsG7uaR_6hEo7ilnF39kr4wI2Z3RnoeskYNzuTRotyzswzqM_eRuOaluGUnkG5eDtQ9nE_IQNUWa_1z3btMhJc-EuS5miVjvGWE2c1OuU-mNklNj5WwFoLBs8QSB_V-pxFJNxDbXhLQUtrtN801OpYiG3ceenZVVaGcb20kSdQrylWiUerIL4yLVUFoRipALMrbuBYp20Zy9U4XbbtAl-WnxtwpHTTh9N3xRZBDinOf-eNjrE2A0NNx7EWVkKVnte2N9v8J5xR9yymY8t92aPuVc4Yvw_Nqkim68q-MU0YaZ3XXZkbj_Okgc-9rWDua0ENpLAnZG_aan2GihCbjHxSEVE1_YXGidFUxA5_Q-2ZO90UGOONKVWVmTAPSr9s3JHw4WAM7TzaMq7LL1NmYd6CpCNhpHZVciPpbUL4obCqhAvLiQdsiARJ4n8gnlqLan_jJkiHWJq0wGBbcrqEzZaFqXCXWKCBmGXy5A4M1jLBmfNczJr1KLedTnnSk4eQZQqHkJDBeuqz9im8Wja24CPEW4w%3D)
---
We're in 3,300.

That's roughly 13% of all high schools in America.

Eight states have officially partnered with Club America to bring our chapters into every school statewide.

✅ Florida
✅ Texas
✅ Tennessee
✅ Oklahoma
✅ Montana
✅ Nebraska
✅ Arkansas
✅ Indiana

And we're just getting started.

Think about that: 13% of America's youth now have a place at school where they can say it's okay to love this country...

That it's okay to be bold. That it's okay to believe in God, in family, and in freedom.

_That 's what Club America is about... _

**Giving the next generation a place where they can find their courage, develop grit, and learn how to lead the fight for their country. **
---
[](http://links.makingamericathegreatest.com/u/click?_t=79fa4a3daf024a0a886c5b498ff32e32&_m=01208e16dbd1403e8dbedb08129441e7&_e=ciw7abm-rOia2M7TJmU8QUCMCIaNeTdfoJ09H_o3RasJu6S-BVezgRAslPWVhQ5VWtxz0J66uQj8hEhPIaiVCaAMwkxQDpBiP8gAf8zEbvVMbCG_W6usKbmX7nGuJnoKRBOR3BIF_N8aA7N67n2KsnIvgtr6UGsMvczAaYVvLZi9bqWL1GwliiXzWSckJme9OfU2C-LWq-0o0MXl0MvsG7uaR_6hEo7ilnF39kr4wI2Z3RnoeskYNzuTRotyzswzqM_eRuOaluGUnkG5eDtQ9uQj2TlsJfr0BujF1JlOQvyejdWehrHFJJo_xGIQghlonFhf6aXcQW0XJi796Fyn3Ahvbe0EX2ZHdOn3Bj3GxBSKHSlWMISrVaOH7vBfUVTPMBggcklp72l1N8TQ8_CYcdXrOqQ3RxeSwPf-JbA0IBerudaiThxYuJwwaQh8HYuT2HjQEIJRa-SShBcbYqNyGVmkFh6liGebiUwShIbU-g7hZN4As6FS4r5sivAI2HnbTR_g4HdhRtL_tjlMKkFBvqFW2iT-oveX_AW_pSoJeDToMYfxicVFwF-mUHQk-BiWh01SIFCenYjcBi9eryok4KS185DQQk8BJGX6GBgH0Qc6P4164c1FXw2YnprlC9lV_XoqK0L4VkYoQ_5R70q-P-0m-kUc3zNmhBLgrM-2VPdeB1Dv1_77_Z80XEaRWdPSLB4ySG7EWxEVAuK7x5iopoWN_YRqxi9VFs_y2kG50cs%3D)
---
_But now, Friend, the question is... _

**What will it take to bring Club America to the next 3,300 schools? What will it take to bring it to all 27,000? **

Because here's the truth:

These students aren't just signing up. _They 're stepping up. _

They're leading chapters in schools where America is attacked... where they're often targeted for daring to say what they believe... and where speaking the truth is dangerous.

But that isn't stopping them.

They're still showing up. They're speaking out. And they're growing stronger than ever.

They're becoming exactly the kind of young patriots Charlie believed in -- not just bold, _but brave_. Not just loud, but _principled_.

**Every time a student starts a new chapter, we make sure they 're not standing alone. **

**We send them an activism kit -- American flags, pocket Constitutions, chapter materials, and leadership tools. **

These kits give student leaders everything they need to rally their peers and stand strong on their campuses.

Each one costs just $25 to pack and ship.

**[If you’re able to, I hope you’ll help send a kit to the next student who raises their hand to lead by making your gift to Turning Point USA today.](http://links.makingamericathegreatest.com/u/click?_t=79fa4a3daf024a0a886c5b498ff32e32&_m=01208e16dbd1403e8dbedb08129441e7&_e=ciw7abm-rOia2M7TJmU8QUCMCIaNeTdfoJ09H_o3RasJu6S-BVezgRAslPWVhQ5VWtxz0J66uQj8hEhPIaiVCaAMwkxQDpBiP8gAf8zEbvVMbCG_W6usKbmX7nGuJnoKRBOR3BIF_N8aA7N67n2KsnIvgtr6UGsMvczAaYVvLZi9bqWL1GwliiXzWSckJme9OfU2C-LWq-0o0MXl0MvsG7uaR_6hEo7ilnF39kr4wI2Z3RnoeskYNzuTRotyzswzqM_eRuOaluGUnkG5eDtQ9kffgu6-Se7OAZ2bpTeZbE0u8-JtsfTyqEwEWPACuhEaZKCYhMkC4XUgAGKh0r7trYq6S0NPX9Xf6ncfFWbew6_MNBLXEpMKORoDEp3U_NS2vV1R5J1buyvoWiXZWeUMflG4n8Q5GSINIxms0WZTeaJzbZj1Ou-CNu2gaI3j7zIEx7zqKm7ooCf9vsVhfh7nTSl2Oc4XGsJu2rWbjMZHpSffryrFtGspaO9IvkiTt0VKz6X-i_D5EsgqLNU7r-ai4Sc-RYwxQRlGh3O1qAcZRF-bUmTX4g1yXAVDAmp1o8wPES7TY3obABmyekfce7Wa7zzuN7Dr9wESSWqGJd5letTSmGpUUDeIzi19ZZbW713dXOuwXIZjaynTtThIUMEYAm13RMj-7Z4EAn8EQEYE3Y13tjToZkvFZ8RyUCtT3ldRHT3a-Eawn3QjsDo1-I89FCTKR-TR5pkuO4fbHAwOxco%3D)**

name: Andy Matthews
subject: Endorsement alert
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY ANDY FOR NEVADA
body:
Our campaign continues to build momentum... | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/andyfornevada/friday-weekly-5859805?e=6736d7bc47)
---
| | [ ](https://us.list-manage.com/1A73L5b9mmZ?e=6736d7bc47&c2id=6d83a76682c29c59feb3e3d11de85f73)
---
| | Dear Peter,

I’ve got some big news for you today, my friend. The state’s largest newspaper, the _Las Vegas Review-Journal_ , has announced it is endorsing me in my re-election campaign for Nevada Controller.

Here’s what the _RJ_ ’s editors write:

_Mr. Matthews, who previously served two years in the Assembly, has represented Nevada well as its chief fiscal officer. He is a stalwart proponent of transparency and created the “state checkbook,” which allows taxpayers to access online detailed information on state outlays. He hopes to use his second term to persuade local governments to do the same. Mr. Matthews has also championed the creation of a state inspector general to conduct forensic audits of state departments in search of waste or fraud. He favors subjecting public-sector collective bargaining to the open meeting law, an excellent idea. ..._

_Voters should enthusiastically support**Andy Matthews.**_

You can read the full write-up [here](https://us.list-manage.com/czCUF7KMyuF?e=6736d7bc47&c2id=6d83a76682c29c59feb3e3d11de85f73).

I’m honored to receive the paper’s endorsement, which is just the latest of many as my campaign continues to build strong momentum for these final weeks. Earlier, I was honored to receive the endorsements of the [Vegas Chamber](https://us.list-manage.com/1D6B1WpRuku?e=6736d7bc47&c2id=6d83a76682c29c59feb3e3d11de85f73) and the [Latin Chamber of Commerce](https://us.list-manage.com/hdncUGisdPK?e=6736d7bc47&c2id=6d83a76682c29c59feb3e3d11de85f73), as well as Citizens for Responsible Government, Nevada Right to Life, and others. Nevada’s Independent American Party has also announced it’s recommending me for re-election.

By the way, I wanted to let you know we’ve also launched a couple of new TV ads highlighting my commitment to government transparency. The ads are similar, as you’ll notice, and we’re targeting them at swing voters in Nevada’s two largest counties.

[This one](https://us.list-manage.com/DjK1CH9CIA8?e=6736d7bc47&c2id=6d83a76682c29c59feb3e3d11de85f73) is running in Washoe County, touting my work in helping local leaders put their county checkbook online.

And [this one](https://us.list-manage.com/173SoMlYzo4?e=6736d7bc47&c2id=6d83a76682c29c59feb3e3d11de85f73) is running in Clark County, and includes my pledge to work with leaders to do the same there in my second term.

We’re trying to get these ads in front of as many eyeballs as possible, and so I hope you’ll consider a contribution to help us do exactly that.

[You can contribute by clicking here.](https://us.list-manage.com/4ZQWyiECKGI?e=6736d7bc47&c2id=6d83a76682c29c59feb3e3d11de85f73)

Well, that’s all for now. As always, thank you for standing with me in my fight to make Nevada’s government more transparent and accountable to the hard-working taxpayers like you who fund it.

Take care, and I’ll see you next time!

For Nevada’s future,

Andy

_Rick and Conor talk Trump and the 2026 campaign_
Rick Telesz is a retired dairy farmer who lives north of Pittsburgh. He is both a lifelong Democrat and someone who voted for Trump. Having long realized he was "conned," Rick decided to run for the statehouse this year as a Democrat. In Pennsylvania, the Democrats control the state house by one seat, and they don't control the state Senate -- so races like Rick's are vitally important. While this is normally a tough seat for us to win, Rick's Republican opponent, the incumbent Aaron Bernstine, was recently stripped of his committees in Harrisburg because of a [homophobic outburst](https://substack.com/redirect/1f1530f2-6b32-42c7-94a4-a50cfb73c920?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). The news coverage around the scandal has injected new life into Rick's campaign and brought victory within reach.
You can support Rick [here](https://substack.com/redirect/7f261792-595f-4222-9198-7a6c8184b501?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). In a race like this one, which could be decided by a few hundred votes, even small donations make an enormous difference. They can help Rick get extra signs and palm cards in the closing weeks, which might give him just enough name recognition to get over the top in this rural district. I try not to bother you too often on behalf of candidates, but Rick is exactly the kind of person we need serving in public office. He's honest, humble, and has no agenda other than to try to make life more affordable for the next generation. He also happens to be a more credible voice on agriculture than we normally have on our side. It would be an enormous achievement to elect him this fall.
Thank you and Happy Sunday!

Friend, We live in the richest country in the world: No one should go hungry, or go bankrupt from medical emergencies, or die because they can’t get healthcare. **But Trump’s Big Brutal Bill cuts are coming into effect, and life’s about to get a lot less affordable for families who’ve already been struggling to afford the basics.** If you use SNAP or Medicaid, or if you get your health insurance from your state’s ACA marketplace or exchange, please know that rising costs and requirements are coming up. Some states will not be able to pay; some will pass this cost to struggling local governments. Refugees and some other previously eligible non-citizens are losing access to SNAP and** Affordable Care Act(ACA) subsidies , which help cover the cost of health insurance. Some immigrants will also face more challenges and restrictions when trying to access Medicaid, CHIP, and Medicare. Re-enrollment and open enrollment is coming up for people who get their health insurance through their state’s exchange or marketplace , which was set up by the Affordable Care Act. Please pay attention in this year’s re-enrollment period: Some people will get a smaller ACA subsidy, some people’s subsidies will be cancelled, and some states are dropping certain plans. You may need to change your plan, which may affect which of your prescriptions or providers are covered. Some people will be forced to drop their plan — priced out of health insurance, as millions were over the past year. And starting in January, Medicaid recipients will need to provide their eligibility every six months, and work reporting requirements will also get stricter. Some states are unfortunately tightening up work reporting requirements earlier than is necessary. These changes are outrageous, but I want to make sure you’re informed. Here are the changes happening this month and the next few months, by early 2027: Many recipients of SNAP food assistance now face more requirements to work, volunteer, or go to school for more time to be able to keep their benefits — including people who are 55-64 years old, people with 14-17 year-old children, and unhoused people. clean_body: I found the fraud, now I'm the target The dubbed "Stop Nick Shirley Act" was made to stop me. | | | | | | | Friend, There's now a law in California with my name associated with it. Everyone in Sacramento knows exactly what the "Stop Nick Shirley Act" means. On August 22nd, Governor Newsom signed AB 2624. Three days later, I was standing at the State Capitol with a crowd of people who showed up because they understood what this law actually does. Supporters say it protects immigration workers from harassment. Here's what it really does, Friend: it makes it harder for anyone -- me included -- to investigate where your tax dollars are being sent. I said it plainly at the rally: this is not the end; this is just the beginning. Because here's the part that should bother you more than anything else. The assemblymember who wrote this bill is married to California's Attorney General -- the one person in this state whose entire job is supposed to be going after fraud. Instead, his wife wrote the bill that makes it harder to expose it. That's not a coincidence, Friend. That's the system protecting itself. I've spent the last year showing up where legacy media won't -- daycare centers, tax-funded nonprofits, the offices of people who'd rather I disappear than answer a question. That work is exactly why a state legislature decided to write a law with my name on it instead of going after the fraud I keep finding. A state senator at the rally called it unconstitutional. A city attorney called it a direct threat to the First Amendment. They're right -- and they're not going to be the ones who stop it. That's going to take people willing to fund the reporters still asking the questions. Here's something most people don't see, Friend: doing this work independently means there's no network paying for the flight to Sacramento, no legal department covering me if a state files a complaint over a story, no corporate budget for the cameras and editors it takes to get this footage in front of you. When I showed up at that rally, Lincoln Media Foundation was on site with their own journalists to cover it, because they understood what was actually at stake before most of the country did. That 's why I'm partnering with Lincoln Media Foundation. They understand how important it is to support independent journalists and help us keep doing the work without compromising what makes it independent in the first place. I'm grateful for their partnership and commitment, and - helping cover travel, equipment, and the costs that come with confronting people on camera instead of reading a press release about them. Since LMF is a 501(c)3, your gift is tax-deductible , and it can be made anonymously if that's what you'd prefer. Friend, they can pass all the laws they want. They can try to prevent people like me from exposing their corruption, that's why it crucial to support independent journalists like myself. They are creating laws to silence free speech -- and that's why we need to continue the fight and I need your support. People like you decide this work is worth funding, and it helps me continue! For the truth, Nick Shirley P.S. -- A California assemblyman is already asking the DOJ to intervene against this law. | | | | Peter, If you want to know exactly how the federal government is managing the lands _you_ own, just follow the money. In Minnesota, the Trump administration is aggressively pushing to allow a toxic sulfide-ore mine right next to the pristine Boundary Waters. The foreign mining company getting the green light **just happens to be owned by a Chilean billionaire who provides a luxury residence to the President’s daughter.** It turns out the going rate for risking the most visited wilderness area in the United States is a nice rental property. You really can't make this stuff up. [**Before we go on, can we count on you to pitch in $3 or more today to our October rapid-response war chest so we can drag these corrupt backroom deals into the light?**](https://go.sparkpostmail1.com/f/a/87N0wZz-DvE_jtmVXc-_3Q~~/AAUS1hA~/zYns1q6XPg69sfX9tvZPcn3RfASt8vewYhelmGL50ENGVKfQe_0ZWLC2EI62ZRyXnoQXCh6X04iU-XTBSByUBNSqB9JDBqX1eQR7rEBDBlxbZ8xmbfBiBfFfzrdmKV4uuFMinLaWEiFaHU9CkiEJin4JXrUOqNFR0AbHkR527_slb_fHHbSlyRTf96ihNDG7jqjAAa7CL-z2C93NZie8rswbtNqK4Vw6JKTMpSJ5B0YN-XPmy4jyee5pB3E-113L) **[**DONATE »** ](https://go.sparkpostmail1.com/f/a/vsKjKZb4mhdt6gMo73PF3Q~~/AAUS1hA~/WQxPWK_4gFe2_UXk4Se5rLpLNUGRj_M1eL3pXo-OHcp2XJy8XreMiEsf8VE6FhO-8mbxlmm-S1oPdWX2e9gFuEHywToiex7s511qepLjNqMkwU6rJ4svXTI5cUlol0Evs6aC0tCYsOd23nzqcquozm7eIdFUlHST4KU1hBk11kClZHAj47DgYVEQXo90j7qihqywEADafc5u2D_JC3wQGywa7rFkKDZJyMrkMz2pGrPUcokHPamhb5HdZgLTn7TR) ** The Boundary Waters is just the tip of the spear. The sheer scale of the theft they are attempting across the country is staggering:
* **Out West:** They slashed Bears Ears and Grand Staircase-Escalante by 90% so mining executives could immediately stake uranium claims on sacred archaeological sites.
* **In our National Forests:** They repealed the Roadless Rule, stripping protections from 45 million acres of untouched landscapes just so the timber lobby can clear-cut the backcountry.
* **Down South:** They are waiving environmental laws to bulldoze through sensitive ecosystems, decimating Organ Pipe National Monument and threatening Big Bend for a vanity border wall.

They are robbing us of our national heritage and expecting us to just sit back and take it. They think their billionaire backers have already bought this victory, and they believe they’re untouchable. **We have exactly 62 days until Election Day to prove them wrong.** At Public Land Warriors, we aren't just writing polite letters of complaint. We are building a targeted, inescapable digital ad blitz to hit the airwaves in the home districts of the politicians who are cheering on this destruction. We are going to offer a very clear perspective to the voters in their districts: exactly who these politicians sold them out to. [**Will you pitch in $3, $25, or $50 today to help us fund the backlash and hold these politicians accountable at the ballot box?**](https://go.sparkpostmail1.com/f/a/vsKjKZb4mhdt6gMo73PF3Q~~/AAUS1hA~/WQxPWK_4gFe2_UXk4Se5rLpLNUGRj_M1eL3pXo-OHcp2XJy8XreMiEsf8VE6FhO-8mbxlmm-S1oPdWX2e9gFuEHywToiex7s511qepLjNqMkwU6rJ4svXTI5cUlol0Evs6aC0tCYsOd23nzqcquozm7eIdFUlHST4KU1hBk11kClZHAj47DgYVEQXo90j7qihqywEADafc5u2D_JC3wQGywa7rFkKDZJyMrkMz2pGrPUcokHPamhb5HdZgLTn7TR) **[**DONATE »** ](https://go.sparkpostmail1.com/f/a/vsKjKZb4mhdt6gMo73PF3Q~~/AAUS1hA~/WQxPWK_4gFe2_UXk4Se5rLpLNUGRj_M1eL3pXo-OHcp2XJy8XreMiEsf8VE6FhO-8mbxlmm-S1oPdWX2e9gFuEHywToiex7s511qepLjNqMkwU6rJ4svXTI5cUlol0Evs6aC0tCYsOd23nzqcquozm7eIdFUlHST4KU1hBk11kClZHAj47DgYVEQXo90j7qihqywEADafc5u2D_JC3wQGywa7rFkKDZJyMrkMz2pGrPUcokHPamhb5HdZgLTn7TR) ** Teddy Roosevelt had the foresight to protect these wild spaces so our kids could experience them. _**by[Lawrence Winnerman](https://substack.com/redirect/a29a325f-f60c-4309-aeb1-98ff21edc8a3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**_
_**Cliff 's Note:**_
##### A guy with an AI subscription built free clones of seven Adobe apps in about a week. Lawrence Winnerman spent twenty-five years inside Microsoft and Amazon, and he knows exactly what this is: Napster, round two. He's also seen who walked away with the money last time.

_**-- Cliff**_
* * *
On September 30, a developer named Brandon Thomas started posting code to GitHub. Within a week he had 7 repositories up, each a free, open-source stand-in for an Adobe product: Photoshop, Illustrator, Premiere Pro, Lightroom, After Effects, InDesign, and Acrobat. He wrote them in Rust, a coding language, with Anthropic's Claude Opus 5.5, a model that had been on sale for 8 days when he started. He says he "one-shotted Photoshop." That means he gave the AI tool one detailed instruction, and then let it run until it was complete. Adobe charges $69.99 a month for the suite. The clones cost nothing.
For now, they are also kind of a mess. The Gaussian blur in the Photoshop clone misbehaves, and the project's own README admits it is "not yet a Photoshop replacement for daily professional work." Adobe will lean on that sentence for as long as it stays true. I give it until Thanksgiving.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/d6fb8814-0a0c-4c56-9df3-780592e57fba?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Eric S. Raymond, the open-source elder, looked at the repos and guessed Thomas must have decompiled Adobe's code, turned it into a specification, and had the machine write fresh Rust from the spec. "Adobe just got nuked," he wrote. "And closed source is dead, dead, dead." The project says otherwise. It calls itself a clean-room reimplementation, built from public specifications and observed behavior, with no Adobe code anywhere in it.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/d6fb8814-0a0c-4c56-9df3-780592e57fba?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
People have argued all week about which version is true, and the argument misses what matters, because the clean-room version is the scarier one for Adobe. Clean-room cloning has been legal in this country for 40 years. In the early 1980s, Compaq spent about $1 million having one team describe what IBM's BIOS did and a second team, which had never seen IBM's code, write new code to match. Phoenix Technologies did the same in 1984 and sold the result to anyone who wanted it. In 1992 the Ninth Circuit ruled in Sega v. Accolade that taking a program apart to learn how it works can be fair use. Copyright protects the code. It does not protect what the code does.
What protected Photoshop all these years was the payroll. Cloning it meant a building full of engineers and several years of their lives, and nobody sane would spend that to give the result away. That bill now fits on a credit card. And if Thomas did decompile something, he broke a license agreement, which makes him a defendant.
[Leave a comment](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=3722532&post_id=219880115&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&isFreemail=true&comments=true&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MjE5ODgwMTE1LCJpYXQiOjE3OTE3MzM5MjAsImV4cCI6MTc5NDMyNTkyMCwiaXNzIjoicHViLTM3MjI1MzIiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.UP7ETD35qBsZqpdjKvXE3aaZOoPXP30hRD0RdAUmMEE&r=1hvr60&utm_campaign=email-half-magic-comments&action=post-comment)
Adobe can sue Brandon Thomas. It cannot sue every kid with a $200 AI subscription and a long weekend.
The games went first, and they show where this is going to end up. Fans spent 6 years, starting in July 2020, decompiling Super Smash Bros. Melee by hand; AI tools helped close out the last stretch, and the project hit 100% on September 7. An unofficial PC port of Fable II, the Xbox 360 game, was running in about an hour with a free open-weight model doing the work. One developer ran as many as 15 AI agents for 3 months, burned through more than 600 billion tokens, and rebuilt an unnamed first-person shooter so exactly that 83% of its functions match the original byte for byte. Then he took his earlier posts down. "Corporate America," he wrote, "was here to ruin our fun."

A developer cloned Adobe's suite in a week with an AI model. Napster already showed us who gets paid when the walls come down. | | and | Oct 11| | | ∙| | Preview ---|---|--- | | | ---|---|--- | | | | | | | | | | | | | ---|---|--- by Cliff 's Note: A guy with an AI subscription built free clones of seven Adobe apps in about a week. Lawrence Winnerman spent twenty-five years inside Microsoft and Amazon, and he knows exactly what this is: Napster, round two. He's also seen who walked away with the money last time. That's the kind of insider read your subscription pays for. . -- Cliff On September 30, a developer named Brandon Thomas started posting code to GitHub. Within a week he had 7 repositories up, each a free, open-source stand-in for an Adobe product: Photoshop, Illustrator, Premiere Pro, Lightroom, After Effects, InDesign, and Acrobat. He wrote them in Rust, a coding language, with Anthropic's Claude Opus 5.5, a model that had been on sale for 8 days when he started. He says he "one-shotted Photoshop." That means he gave the AI tool one detailed instruction, and then let it run until it was complete. Adobe charges $69.99 a month for the suite. The clones cost nothing. For now, they are also kind of a mess. The Gaussian blur in the Photoshop clone misbehaves, and the project's own README admits it is "not yet a Photoshop replacement for daily professional work." Adobe will lean on that sentence for as long as it stays true. I give it until Thanksgiving. | | ---|---|--- Eric S. Raymond, the open-source elder, looked at the repos and guessed Thomas must have decompiled Adobe's code, turned it into a specification, and had the machine write fresh Rust from the spec. "Adobe just got nuked," he wrote. "And closed source is dead, dead, dead." The project says otherwise. It calls itself a clean-room reimplementation, built from public specifications and observed behavior, with no Adobe code anywhere in it. | | ---|---|--- People have argued all week about which version is true, and the argument misses what matters, because the clean-room version is the scarier one for Adobe. Clean-room cloning has been legal in this country for 40 years. In the early 1980s, Compaq spent about $1 million having one team describe what IBM's BIOS did and a second team, which had never seen IBM's code, write new code to match. Phoenix Technologies did the same in 1984 and sold the result to anyone who wanted it. In 1992 the Ninth Circuit ruled in Sega v. Accolade that taking a program apart to learn how it works can be fair use. Copyright protects the code. It does not protect what the code does. What protected Photoshop all these years was the payroll. Cloning it meant a building full of engineers and several years of their lives, and nobody sane would spend that to give the result away. That bill now fits on a credit card. And if Thomas did decompile something, he broke a license agreement, which makes him a defendant. Adobe can sue Brandon Thomas. It cannot sue every kid with a $200 AI subscription and a long weekend. The games went first, and they show where this is going to end up. Fans spent 6 years, starting in July 2020, decompiling Super Smash Bros. Melee by hand; AI tools helped close out the last stretch, and the project hit 100% on September 7. An unofficial PC port of Fable II, the Xbox 360 game, was running in about an hour with a free open-weight model doing the work. One developer ran as many as 15 AI agents for 3 months, burned through more than 600 billion tokens, and rebuilt an unnamed first-person shooter so exactly that 83% of its functions match the original byte for byte. Then he took his earlier posts down. "Corporate America," he wrote, "was here to ruin our fun." Literally as I was writing this, a story broke on Twitter (X) that drives the stake deeper into the heart of traditional software giants..** Continue reading this post for free in the Substack app | | | | | | | (C) 2026 Cliff Schecter PO Box 8384, Cincinnati, OH 45208 ? ?

| **Math Matters** :** The Cost of Janoo’s ‘Free’ Healthcare Plan **

New reports raise fundamental questions about Amanda Janoo’s promise to deliver “free” universal primary care.

According to an October 8th VTDigger story, **[she doesn’t know how much it will cost or how care will be delivered [1].](https://us.list-manage.com/1CHvCeLQ9RV?e=19cebfe173&c2id=84d1094b3a168b6495ef78aca9f3540c "https://vtdigger.org/2026/10/08/universal-primary-care-is-at-the-center-of-the-race-for-governor-how-would-it-work/")**

She says she has lots of “estimates.” But never mentions which additional taxes she will raise on Vermonters when the new tax she has identified falls far short.

**_WHAT DOES THE REAL MATH SHOW?_**

A 2016 report from Governor Peter Shumlin’s (D) administration to the Legislature estimated “free” universal primary care would cost between $294.1 million and $316.6 million [2].

Adjusted for Vermont’s medical inflation since 2017, those costs rise to between $580 million and $611 million.

Amanda Janoo’s “wealth tax” – by her own estimates – raises between $114 million and $344 million. _(Side note: She currently proposes to put new income taxes on filers beginning at $250,000 of combined annual income, because she does not believe these households and small businesses pay their “fair share.”)_

**Right out of the gate, her promise starts off $250 million - $500 million in the negative. **

That’s not decimal dust. It would be one of the single largest tax increases in state history.

**Janoo told VTDigger she’s open to “exploring an array of options for funding the program...” _ But never specifies which ones._**

**_WILL IT LOWER COSTS FOR VERMONTERS?_**

Janoo argues that a government-run and taxpayer-funded “free” universal primary care system will save you money by “lowering hospitalizations and reliance on specialty services.”

She describes her savings projections as “a rough estimate intended to gauge whether an ambitious plan for primary care would be feasible and financeable.”

But she never actually shows you the math.

A UVM healthcare policy professor told VTDigger:

**_“I have not seen a lot of evidence that would then lead to markedly fewer expensive specialist visits or emergency room visits.” _**

And:

**_“I am not convinced that this particular idea would have a major return on investment that would justify raising taxes and increasing spending on health care.” _**

**HAVEN’T WE SEEN THIS MOVIE BEFORE?**

Yes. Vermont has been through this exact thing before.

In fact, Vermonters are still paying more, and have fewer choices, because of the same inflexible ideological commitment to an idea that the math – and Democratic party leaders like Governor Peter Shumlin – determined was unworkable at the state level, just 12 years ago.

Voters (and reporters) who were not here for that, or who are under 30, should google:

“Governor Shumlin and Single Payer” for a refresher.

Spoiler alert: Governor Shumlin canceled the plan after years of work because the taxes required were, in his words, “enormous” and the economic consequences too significant.

**WHAT’S GOVERNOR SCOTT’S PLAN?**

Governor Phil Scott wants Vermonters to have universally accessible and affordable healthcare – but has a more affordable, more immediate, and more mainstream plan to get there.

In June, Governor Scott signed Act 173, directing further study on a universal primary care system. When he signed it, he said any universal primary care plan must accomplish critical policy goals:
* Improve access while reducing overall healthcare costs.
* Protect primary care providers, especially in rural communities.
* Strengthen Vermont’s economic growth and economic competitiveness.
* Be something young families and working Vermonters can easily use and truly afford – because no matter what candidates promise on the campaign trail... it won’t be “free.”

The Governor has also, repeatedly, put forward plans to lower healthcare premiums and expand choice – but the supermajority has refused these more affordable, mainstream changes.

His plan uses proven tools – tools virtually every other state is using – available to us through the Affordable Care Act (aka Obamacare) [3].

The same tools allow New Hampshire to offer more plans at a _fraction_ of the cost as Vermont. For example, a family plan can cost Vermonters upwards of $26,000 dollars each year, while in New Hampshire, that same family would pay just $11,000 for the same plan.

If the Legislature passes Governor Scott’s plan, we can protect seniors, increase options, and lower insurance costs for younger workers and families; while restoring affordable options like healthcare co-ops and association plans for small businesses and non-profits.

**Vermonters want real plans and solutions that lower costs NOW. Not another promise of “free” healthcare with no math to pay for it.**

Math matters.

A lot.

_**And with a contribution today, we can continue to shed light on the types of proposals that will cost Vermonters more at a time when we need to do everything we can to make Vermont more affordable, not less.**_ ###

Case File No DRT-ED-SUPPLY · Special File · The New Front Line
Ukraine Didn’t Aim at Tanks. It Burned Russia’s Amazon. Every Business on Earth Just Learned the Lesson.
Since July, Ukrainian drones have hit dozens of warehouses run by Russia’s biggest online retailers. Losses run into the billions, and most of it was uninsured. Modern war goes after supply chains first, and the companies that protect them are moving into the spotlight.
Threat level 4/5 — Elevated
| | | | | | | | |
---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---
|
---
For most of history, wars were fought over armies, borders and cities. This summer, a new kind of target became the headline: warehouses. Not weapons depots. Regular e-commerce warehouses, full of phones, clothes and household goods.
The evidence board
| | What the Drones Did
---|---
| EVIDENCE
---
**Exhibit A — the targets.** The first strikes on Wildberries, which holds about 45% of Russia’s online retail market, came on July 18. Within a month, more than 20 of its warehouses had been hit. In late August, the drones turned to its rival, Ozon.
| EVIDENCE
---
**Exhibit B — the damage.** One Russian outlet estimated that about 43% of Wildberries’ warehouse space was lost. Reuters put it at no less than one-fifth. Forbes Russia estimated sellers’ losses at 215 to 280 billion rubles by early August.
| EVIDENCE
---
**Exhibit C — the fallout.** About 80% of the buildings and inventory were reportedly uninsured. More than 400,000 sellers were affected. Ozon’s shares fell 27% after a string of strikes in August.
| OUR THEORY
---
Ukraine didn’t need to win a battle to hit Russia’s economy. It went after the systems that move goods. Every company, every army and every government watching has now learned the same lesson: **supply chains are the soft target of modern war.**
Why it matters to you
| | Why This Isn’t Just Russia’s Problem
---|---
| →| **Every Western supply chain is exposed.** Ports, warehouses and distribution hubs are just as hard to protect.
---|---
| →| **Budgets follow fear.** When a threat becomes visible, governments and corporations spend to defend against it, fast.
---|---
| →| **The early solutions win.** Companies that already have proven tools tend to capture the first and largest contracts.
---|---
| ClassificationLesson learned
---
The burning warehouses are on Russia’s side of the border, but the wake-up call is global. Protecting logistics has gone from a back-office issue to a national security priority.

subject: Trump's first plan was worse
body:

---
| | | Picture your ballot showing up by certified mail. If you're not home to sign for it, it goes back. According to new reporting from ProPublica, **that's how the Trump White House first wanted mail voting to work.**
---
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/141195081/652754014/-569431239?refcode=261011-mail&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDcvMS83NzI2MCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIyZjYxODk1Ni04Y2M1LWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDBkM2E0ZmJlODMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=KcIGoyguYOecE2PbxgtlYkypF599k_s_1R_VKWShIgI=)
---
The administration floated a plan to require every ballot to be delivered by certified mail. It was dropped only after the Postal Service warned that it would be impossible to carry out. The plan they ended up with was hardly better. Trump's March executive order would have turned postal workers into gatekeepers, deciding which ballots got delivered and which didn't. It put Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, who has no formal authority over the Postal Service, in charge of coordinating it. Postal officials were left out of key conversations, and the order's contents shocked even the Postal Service's own lawyers. **Then the White House insisted that if even one envelope in a batch didn't match a state's voter list, the whole batch should be rejected.** A former postal official told ProPublica what that would mean: **_"If four addresses don't align in a mailing of one million, 999,996 other people don't get their ballot tomorrow."_** Oregon votes entirely by mail. In our state, that would not cause a “glitch” – it would have resulted in our election grinding to a halt. The Supreme Court blocked the order last month. But the reporting makes one thing clear: this was never just a careless mistake. It took nearly a year of planning by people who knew exactly how much disruption they were designing. **They won't stop at one order. As your Secretary of State, I'm going to keep Oregon's vote-by-mail system working for every eligible voter, no matter what the Trump Administration tries next. To do that, I need people standing with me before the next attack comes.** **[Can you chip in $15 to my campaign right now and help us stand up to Trump's attacks on vote-by-mail? ](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/141195082/652754015/-569431239?refcode=261011-mail&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDcvMS83NzI2MCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIyZjYxODk1Ni04Y2M1LWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDBkM2E0ZmJlODMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=KcIGoyguYOecE2PbxgtlYkypF599k_s_1R_VKWShIgI=)**

I refuse to sit by while people continue to lose access to critical programs.
# [](https://act.sarahmcbride.com/go/1269?t=1&akid=3976%2E21716%2ELMGQhR)
**Last month, the Trump administration canceled Affordable Care Act Marketplace coverage for more than 750,000 Americans.**
They’ve claimed the cancellations are based on fraud or ineligibility, but they’ve provided _zero_ evidence to prove it.
Over 19 million Americans rely on coverage from the Affordable Care Act, with the cost of living — and specifically healthcare costs — continuously increasing across the country.
And for the last two years, Donald Trump and Republicans in Congress have been continually cutting the programs working families rely on so they can give tax breaks to their billionaire friends.
**We even saw DOGE ransack the government while leaving real cases of fraud untouched.** All while neglecting to implement alternatives, leaving the costs of these cuts to fall on the backs of hardworking Americans.
I want to be clear: We absolutely have a duty to deliver accountability and root out waste, fraud, and abuse. But we need to do it without denying our neighbors access to the critical lifelines they desperately need.
In order to keep Delaware’s seat in Congress blue, bring true accountability to this administration, and make sure everyone who needs it has access to crucial programs like the Affordable Care Act, we need to make sure we’re reaching Delawareans up and down the state.

But when thousands of supporters like you chip in $1 when they can, it adds up pretty fast. $1 donations helped me win this district TWICE when I ran in 2018 and 2020. $1 helped me win my primary in August. And $1 will help me defeat Trump’s self-proclaimed “warrior” Jen Kiggans and the MAGA money backing her. On Wednesday at midnight, we file the last fundraising report before Election Day. Our opponents will read the dollar total, but they'll also read how many people contributed to it. They’re trying to buy this House seat. We have thousands of patriots who refuse to let that happen. That’s why I have to ask: = | | | = | | = It might not seem like a lot, but even $1 goes a long way. — Elaine Luria | | We believe that emails are the best way for our campaign to stay in touch with supporters like you. name: Elizabeth Warren
subject: Trump’s secret AI “regulation” plan: Written by Zuck and Musk
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Warren for Senate
body:
I’m demanding answers from Trump’s White House

| | | [ ](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/go/216?t=3&akid=3051%2E4032634%2EAqxhSe)
---
Imagine if the tobacco companies got to decide which cigarettes the FDA was allowed to inspect. Or if Wall Street firms could tell the SEC which trades it could investigate. You’d call that a pretty obvious conflict of interest. Right? So why are we letting the biggest AI companies in the world help decide how they should be regulated? AI is moving too fast for the government to simply hope Big Tech will do the right thing. So the Trump administration, at first, was developing a process to test powerful AI systems for serious security risks. It was kind of a no-brainer if you ask me: before these systems are widely deployed, experts should have a chance to find out whether they could be used to attack our banks, power grid, hospitals, or other critical infrastructure. Then the CEOs got involved. Executives from Google, OpenAI, and Anthropic reportedly objected to parts of the process. And Trump’s buddies Mark Zuckerberg and Elon Musk also raised concerns. And the rules changed. What had been considered a “requirement” is now more of a suggestion. The review process was shortened, and the details still being worked out are being handled behind closed doors. The American people have no oversight or say. The companies that are supposed to be regulated are getting a say in the rules meant to regulate them. And I, for one, am not going to sit back and watch it happen. I’m demanding that the top officials in Trump’s White House release every communication between these companies and the administration about the AI policy. We need to know about their secret AI framework and how it impacts the public. The American people deserve strong guardrails set by democratically elected officials, not a toothless framework shaped in secret by a handful of billionaires. I’m going to keep pushing until we know what happened and the American people can see how these decisions are being made. Thanks for being a part of this, Elizabeth Warren | **Elizabeth Warren has called for an immediate pause on advanced AI development so that Congress can put proper guardrails and regulations in place to prevent serious harm. She has also introduced policies to tax AI companies to prevent an economic collapse, and to make AI companies pay for their own data center usage that is jacking up utility prices.** **If you’re able, pitch in to power this work.** | [**DONATE NOW**](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/go/3841?t=8&akid=3051%2E4032634%2EAqxhSe)
